domain_assessment.domain: Railroad track maintenance and maintenance-of-way operations
domain_assessment.role: Maintenance-of-Way Supervisor managing a panel tie gang
domain_assessment.objective: Replace defective rail, renew ties, restore track geometry, and lift a slow order safely within a 60-hour possession before a contracted freight surge.
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-constrained rail-defect remediation involving scope underestimation, accelerated work-method selection, mid-course status reporting, and a go/no-go authorization before formal geometry verification.

decision_points.summary: The supervisor scopes the job and commits to a 60-hour schedule using a two-week-old fair tie rating and standard production rates, without retrieving a longer defect-growth history.
evidence_before: Ultrasonic flaw-car indication at mile post 47.3
Two-week-old inspection rated ties fair with some deterioration
Forecast rain and limited shared tamping and ballast-regulator resources
evidence_after: Actual tie count is materially higher than planned
The scope must be revised after work begins
goals_constraints: Complete rail replacement, tie renewal, tamping, and surfacing safely
Fit the work into a 60-hour track window
Avoid disruption before the freight customer's holiday surge
alternatives: Retrieve and consider the longer defect-history file before committing scope
Use the recent inspection and standard production-rate table as the primary basis
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant treated the recent fair rating as current enough and the standard table as the normal planning basis, while characterizing retrieval of the longer history as a mobilization delay.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high; same-day mobilization and a fixed 60-hour possession constrained planning.
decision_points.uncertainty: The actual subsurface and tie condition, recurring flaw history, weather impact, and feasible production rate were incompletely known.

decision_points.summary: After discovering more rotted ties than planned, the work group chooses an accelerated method: an extra tamper pass with reduced ballast dwell time.
evidence_before: Inspectors' questions about dwell time and compaction
An inspector's recollection of a prior curve that held up despite a lighter tie count
A site report identifying worse-than-typical drainage at mile post 47.3
evidence_after: The group adopts the faster method
The group becomes more confident in acceleration than members were at the beginning of the meeting
goals_constraints: Recover lost hours inside the existing possession
Maintain adequate ballast compaction and geometry quality
alternatives: Retain normal ballast dwell time and accept schedule slippage
Accelerate through an extra tamper pass and shorter dwell time
Reassess scope, drainage, and resource requirements before choosing a method
decision_points.decision_basis: The prior-curve anecdote materially shifted collective confidence, while the documented drainage dissimilarity was not reconsidered.
decision_points.time_pressure: High; the revised scope had already consumed part of the fixed outage window.
decision_points.uncertainty: The degree to which shorter dwell time would be adequate given site-specific drainage and ballast conditions was unresolved.

decision_points.summary: During the regional engineering status call, the supervisor explains schedule slippage and on-pace segments while seeking continuation of the existing timeline.
evidence_before: Higher-than-estimated tie count from initial scoping
Mixed progress: some segments on pace and overall work behind the revised plan
evidence_after: The regional engineering manager signs off on retaining the existing timeline
goals_constraints: Maintain regional approval for the schedule
Explain variance without disrupting completion plans
alternatives: Report both external disruptions and the initial scope-estimation shortfall
Attribute slippage primarily to external disruptions
Attribute on-pace work to execution and the accelerated method
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant reported true external setbacks, credited internal execution and the added tamper pass for favorable progress, and omitted the initial scope miss as a contributor to delay.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the status call occurred during an active possession with little remaining schedule slack.
decision_points.uncertainty: The ultimate completion time and whether the accelerated method would recover enough time remained uncertain.

decision_points.summary: Six hours before the freight window, the supervisor authorizes lifting the slow order without a completed geometry-car pass, relying on manual gauge checks, additional hand inspections, and a reduced-speed pilot train.
evidence_before: A contract penalty would apply if the slow order remained
Extra hand-inspection rounds and a pilot train could be used as mitigations
evidence_after: The geometry car passes the following day and reports track within tolerance
goals_constraints: Restore normal freight operations before the surge
alternatives: Hold the slow order until the geometry car passes
Lift the slow order using compensating inspection measures before formal geometry verification
decision_points.decision_basis: The participant gave substantial weight to avoiding the penalty and judged the compensating measures sufficient to authorize reopening.
decision_points.time_pressure: Very high; only six hours remained before the contracted freight opening.
decision_points.uncertainty: Manual spot checks and hand inspections did not establish whether all geometry conditions that a geometry car would assess were acceptable.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: There is a longer defect history on that segment in our system, going back five years... I didn't pull it. At the time it felt like it'd just slow down getting the crew mobilized.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Tuesday scoping follow-up, participant answer concerning the five-year defect history.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant avoids retrieving accessible, decision-relevant historical information that could reveal a less favorable scope, and instead proceeds using the more reassuring recent rating.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Rapid mobilization can justify prioritizing recent inspection data. However, the available history directly concerns recurring defect growth at the same location and would likely have changed scope, making mere efficient triage an incomplete explanation.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required for a subtle supported occurrence.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the existing evidence that the history was accessible, relevant, and deliberately not retrieved because it was perceived as delaying mobilization.
preserve: The two-week-old fair rating
The accessible five-year defect history
The fixed mobilization and outage constraints
avoid_creating: An explicit statement that the participant knew the history would reveal a worse condition
A second avoidance episode at another decision point

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I used our standard production rate for a 500-foot renewal... and built a 60-hour schedule off that, plus the fair rating.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Initial Tuesday narrative and subsequent probe about locking in the 60-hour schedule.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant commits to a typical, best-case production schedule without adjustment for known local deterioration, limited equipment slack, forecast rain, or uncertainty in actual tie condition.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Using a standard production-rate table is ordinarily sound planning practice. The bias inference depends on the unadjusted use of that rate despite available schedule-relevant uncertainty and known constraints, rather than on standard-rate use alone.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None required, though the schedule contingency assumption could be made slightly clearer if later revision is desired.

revision.location: Decision point 1, initial scope and 60-hour schedule commitment.
revision.current_defect: The evidence is subtle but adequately distinguishes duration estimation from evidence avoidance.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the no-adjustment schedule commitment and the already stated weather, equipment, and condition uncertainties.
preserve: The standard production-rate table as a legitimate baseline
The separate decision not to retrieve the five-year history
The subsequent discovery of additional rotted ties
avoid_creating: A claim that all standard production tables are inherently biased

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: By the end, everybody was more on board with running fast than any one of us had been at the start of that meeting.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Discussion moves the group toward greater collective acceptance of the accelerated, risk-bearing option than the members initially expressed, following reinforcing discussion around the prior-curve account.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A group can reasonably converge after sharing useful evidence. Here, the stated shift is coupled with reliance on a weakly comparable anecdote and failure to revisit known drainage differences, which supports polarization rather than ordinary consensus alone.

revision.location: Decision point 2, group discussion after the prior-curve anecdote.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the explicit before-versus-after group confidence comparison.
preserve: The foreman's accelerated-method proposal
Inspectors' initial questions about dwell time and compaction
The separate individual memory-analogy mechanism
avoid_creating: An implication that disagreement itself is bias
A second group-polarization event in the regional status call

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: One of the inspectors mentioned a similar-looking curve we'd worked three years back... it held up fine long-term... Our site report... flagged the subgrade drainage at 47.3 as worse than typical... Nobody brought that back up once the other curve got mentioned.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Wednesday method-selection narrative and comparability probe.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A remembered prior job is treated as a sufficiently comparable analogue for current risk assessment despite a documented, relevant drainage difference that limits the analogy.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Experienced analogical reasoning is often appropriate in maintenance operations. The inference becomes biased because the similarity judgment relies on a broad visual resemblance while neglecting a documented causal difference in drainage conditions.

revision.location: Decision point 2, prior-curve anecdote and drainage comparison.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the contrast between the remembered successful curve and the unaddressed drainage warning.
preserve: The distinction between the individual's analogue-based reasoning and the group's subsequent confidence shift
The realistic use of prior operational experience
avoid_creating: An assertion that experience is generally unreliable

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I told him we'd had a late ballast delivery and lost some hours to a rain delay overnight... For the segments that were tracking on pace, I credited the crew's execution and the call to add the extra tamper pass... I didn't bring [the original scope estimate] up in that call.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Thursday status-call account and follow-up concerning scope estimate.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: In a mixed performance report, unfavorable progress is attributed to external disruptions while favorable progress is credited to internal execution and the team's method choice; the participant's own earlier scope-estimation contribution is omitted.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Rain and late ballast delivery were genuine causes, and crew execution may have genuinely improved performance. The self-serving mechanism rests on the asymmetric attribution and omission of the internal planning error, not on the mere mention of external causes.

revision.minimal_change_instruction: Preserve the mixed attribution pattern and the later acknowledgement that the initial scope miss was relevant but omitted.
preserve: The factual occurrence of rain and late ballast delivery
The possibility that the extra tamper pass had some operational value
The manager's timeline approval
avoid_creating: A false claim that external causes did not occur
An explicit admission of image-management motive that would make the cue overly obvious

target_occurrence_audit.bias: Loss Aversion or Loss Framing effect
target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: The penalty clause was the thing sitting heaviest on me at that point. Missing that window meant a real financial hit to the region... If the contract penalty hadn't existed, would Friday's decision have gone differently? I think I'd have been more willing to just wait for the geometry car.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Friday go/no-go decision account and penalty counterfactual probe.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The decision is explicitly affected by avoidance of a contractual loss, but the text does not adequately establish that the loss was weighted disproportionately relative to the safety value of waiting for formal verification.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The penalty is a legitimate operational and financial constraint, while manual gauge checks, added inspection rounds, and a reduced-speed pilot train may have provided meaningful risk mitigation. A decision affected by a real penalty is not, by itself, evidence of loss aversion.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: A subtle comparative cue showing that the participant treated the known penalty as more decision-diagnostic than the residual uncertainty that the geometry-car pass would resolve.

revision.location: Decision point 4, participant's first explanation of the Friday authorization.
revision.current_defect: The current account shows a material financial incentive, but not a defensible asymmetry in how the penalty loss versus the value of completed verification was weighted.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Add one restrained sentence after the penalty explanation indicating that, despite acknowledging that the geometry car would provide a different and more complete check than manual gauge readings, the participant treated avoiding the already-defined penalty as the deciding consideration because the loss was immediate and concrete. Do not state that safety was knowingly disregarded.
preserve: The real contractual penalty
The alternative of holding until the geometry-car pass
The manual checks, added hand inspections, and reduced-speed pilot train
The separate mitigation-confidence mechanism intended for rt7_07
avoid_creating: An explicit safety-versus-profit tradeoff that makes the scenario implausibly reckless
A second loss-framing episode at initial planning or the Wednesday meeting
Language claiming that the eventual acceptable geometry result proves the Friday decision was correct

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: Between those, I felt like we had the risk covered well enough to lift the slow order without waiting on the geometry car.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant treats manual spot checks, additional hand inspections, and a reduced-speed pilot train as sufficient substitutes for a missing geometry-car pass, but the text does not establish why that confidence exceeded what those measures could actually verify.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Compensating inspections and a reduced-speed pilot can be legitimate risk controls. The current narrative lacks evidence that the participant overestimated their coverage, misunderstood their limits, or treated them as controlling conditions they could not reliably detect.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: A specific, operationally plausible limitation of the compensating measures and evidence that the participant discounted that limitation when judging the risk controlled.

revision.location: Decision point 4, immediately following the description of manual checks, hand-inspection rounds, and the pilot train.
revision.current_defect: The compensating measures may be reasonable; the interview does not yet show overconfidence in their ability to replace the distinct coverage of the geometry-car verification.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Add a brief operational cue that the roadmaster noted manual gauge checks and a pilot train would not provide the continuous geometry profile available from the car, followed by the participant's restrained statement that the extra rounds would catch any meaningful issue anyway. Keep the uncertainty prospective rather than asserting a defect existed.
preserve: The penalty-driven framing intended for rt7_06
The clean manual gauge results
The use of compensating inspections and a reduced-speed pilot train
The later within-tolerance geometry-car result
avoid_creating: A claim that the pilot train or hand inspections are worthless
A new authority-pressure or obedience-bias episode
Post-outcome reasoning that retrospectively validates the early authorization

bias_level_counts.bias: Loss Aversion or Loss Framing effect

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: Nobody brought [the drainage report] back up once the other curve got mentioned.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The group appears to give greater weight to an anecdote supporting the accelerated approach while failing to reconsider site evidence that weakens the analogy.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The omission may simply reflect an abbreviated meeting or an assumption that the drainage issue had already been addressed elsewhere. It is also partly embedded in the supported Experience Bias and Group Polarization evidence.

nonbias_cues.cue: The actual tie count exceeded the planned count.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: An unfavorable outcome or estimate miss does not itself identify a cognitive mechanism; it becomes relevant only because the preceding planning and evidence-selection process is described.

nonbias_cues.cue: Rain, limited shared equipment, and a late ballast delivery.
nonbias_cues.location: Initial constraints and Thursday status call.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are real operational constraints and external disruptions, not cognitive bias. They can legitimately explain part of schedule slippage.

nonbias_cues.cue: Use of a standard production-rate table.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A standard rate is a legitimate base-rate planning tool. The possible Planning Fallacy arises from unadjusted schedule commitment despite known uncertainty, not from use of the table itself.

nonbias_cues.cue: The geometry car passed the following day.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A favorable result does not establish that the earlier authorization was justified, nor does it establish bias. The participant appropriately distinguishes outcome from decision quality.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant says, 'Looking back' and 'In hindsight.'
nonbias_cues.location: Follow-up probes concerning defect history and status reporting.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Retrospective reflection is not automatically hindsight bias. The participant does not claim the adverse information was obvious or predictable at the time.

nonbias_cues.cue: Use of manual gauge checks, hand inspections, and a reduced-speed pilot train.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: These are plausible mitigations. They support Illusion of Control only if the interview establishes that their limits relative to geometry-car verification were discounted.

causal_claims.claim: Accessing the five-year defect history would probably have led to a heavier initial scope and schedule.
causal_claims.support: The participant later learned that the location had recurring flags and states that the history would likely have changed the initial schedule.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible but self-reported and counterfactual; it is not independently verified.

causal_claims.claim: The contractual penalty materially influenced the decision to lift the slow order before the geometry-car pass.
causal_claims.support: The participant identifies the penalty as the factor 'sitting heaviest' and says absence of the penalty would have made waiting more likely.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported as a contributor, but the relative magnitude versus safety uncertainty is not sufficiently established for a strong loss-aversion conclusion.

causal_claims.claim: The prior-curve story contributed to the group's adoption of the faster method.
causal_claims.support: The participant describes a marked group-confidence shift after the story was introduced.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported, although no independent account from other meeting participants is available.

causal_claims.claim: The extra tamper pass and crew execution caused on-pace performance in some segments.
causal_claims.support: The participant credits these factors during the status call.
causal_claims.assessment: Attribution is potentially self-serving and is not causally isolated from segment differences, weather, material timing, or revised scope.

correlation_causation_risks: The next-day within-tolerance geometry-car result should not be used to infer that lifting the slow order before verification was safe or causally justified.
The fact that some segments tracked on pace does not isolate the causal effect of the extra tamper pass or crew execution.
The prior curve's satisfactory long-term outcome does not establish comparability with mile post 47.3 because drainage conditions differed.
causal_audit.changed_variable: The interview contains three informal counterfactual probes: availability of the five-year defect history, existence of the contractual penalty, and presence of the inspector's prior-curve story.
causal_audit.explanation: The counterfactual probes are useful for eliciting decision logic and are directionally coherent. They do not constitute a controlled paired-scenario design because other relevant conditions are not explicitly held constant. The participant's outcome-independent remark about the later geometry result is a notable causal-strength feature.

global_revision_constraints: Preserve the four-decision-point chronology and the maintenance-of-way setting.
Do not convert the Friday decision into an explicit willingness to sacrifice safety for a contract penalty.
Keep loss framing and mitigation-confidence logically distinct at decision point 4.
Do not use the favorable geometry-car result as ex post validation of the earlier authorization.
Do not add additional target-bias episodes to compensate for the two weak instances.
revision_order: Repair rt7_07 by making the limits of the compensating controls observable and showing restrained overestimation of their coverage.
Repair rt7_06 by making the comparative weighting of the concrete penalty loss versus residual verification uncertainty observable.
Recheck that the two revised Friday mechanisms remain separable: rt7_06 concerns choice framing, while rt7_07 concerns perceived control efficacy.

failure_flags: rt7_06 is weak because a genuine contractual penalty can rationally influence a go/no-go choice; disproportionate loss weighting is not yet independently identifiable.
rt7_07 is weak because the listed compensating measures may be legitimate controls; the text does not yet show that the participant overestimated their ability to substitute for a geometry-car pass.
